record.paper_title: High Open-Circuit Voltages in Lead-Halide Perovskite Solar Cells – Experiment, Theory and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Interface tradeoff between recombination and extraction
record.original_question: How can perovskite solar-cell interfaces and electron or hole transport layers be optimized when low surface recombination velocity may improve open-circuit voltage, but the same contact-layer choices may increase series resistance or create an electric-field distribution that makes charge extraction at the maximum power point more difficult?

evidence.quote: While low values of S guarantee high open-circuit voltages, what counts for efficiency is Vmpp which may be reduced drastically by higher series resistances. This illustrates that contact layers not only have to ensure low S but also low Rs.

The low surface recombination velocities of organic electron and hole transport layers might bring about a fundamental compromise between recombination, resistive losses and optimization of the electric field distribution in the device [43,44]. As shown in Fig. 3, a low value of S might benefit Voc but if it comes with a high value of Rs, the efficiency might be reduced. The same holds true if the electric field distribution is such that it makes charge extraction more difficult, because most of the electric field drops over the electron and hole transport layers [43,44]. Thus, we need a better understanding of resistive and charge collection losses at interfaces and in electron and hole transport layers.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a thin-film solar cell consisting of an absorber layer of thickness $d$ sandwiched between an electron transport layer (ETL) and a hole transport layer (HTL), each characterized by a surface recombination velocity $S$ (cm/s) at the absorber/transport-layer interface and contributing to a total series resistance $R_s$ (Ω·cm$^2$). Under standard one-sun illumination, the cell's current–voltage characteristic can be modeled by
$$ J(V) \;=\; J_{	ext{ph}} \;-\; J_0\!\left(\exp\! rac{q(V+J R_s)}{n k_B T}-1ight) \;-\;  rac{V+J R_s}{R_{sh}}, $$
where $J_{	ext{ph}}$ is the photogenerated current density, $J_0$ is the saturation current density (which depends on $S$ through the effective recombination at both interfaces, e.g. $J_0 \propto S$ in the surface-recombination-limited regime), $n$ is the ideality factor, $T$ the temperature, $R_{sh}$ the shunt resistance, and $q,k_B$ have their usual meanings. The open-circuit voltage is $V_{oc} = V$ such that $J(V)=0$, and the maximum-power-point voltage $V_{mpp}$ maximizes $V\cdot J(V)$. In addition, the spatial distribution of the built-in electric field across the absorber and the transport layers — determined by the dielectric permittivities, doping densities, and band offsets of ETL/HTL — modulates the effective collection efficiency $\eta_c \in (0,1]$ multiplying $J_{	ext{ph}}$, with most of the potential dropping over the transport layers when those layers are weakly doped or thick.

Formulate and solve the following optimization problem: choose the transport-layer parameters (thickness, doping density, dielectric constant, band offset, and resulting interface surface recombination velocity $S$) so as to maximize the power conversion efficiency
$$ \eta \;=\;  rac{\max_V \, V\,J(V)}{P_{	ext{in}}}, $$
subject to the trade-off that decreasing $S$ (which raises $V_{oc}$) generally increases $R_s$ and may redistribute the electric field in a way that reduces $\eta_c$ at $V_{mpp}$. Specifically: (i) derive analytic conditions characterizing the optimal $(S, R_s, \eta_c)$ triple for which $V_{mpp}\cdot J(V_{mpp})$ is maximized, and (ii) determine quantitatively how the resistive and field-distribution losses at the ETL/HTL interfaces should be balanced against the recombination losses in order to achieve the highest attainable efficiency.
artifact.status_search_result: The interplay between interface recombination velocity, series resistance, and electric-field distribution in perovskite solar cells remains an active topic in device physics. While many partial models (drift-diffusion simulations, equivalent-circuit analyses) have been developed, no closed-form joint optimization of $S$, $R_s$, and field-distribution losses for ETL/HTL design has been broadly accepted, and reviews continue to list it as an open device-engineering problem.

status_evidence.claim: Authors explicitly identify the trade-off between low S, low R_s, and favorable field distribution as an open question.
